designSummary: Single-clinic implementation study with baseline and adapted group cohorts; completion plotted by group on a run chart, with descriptive comparison of reach and outcomes.
sampleSize: About 120 people start the programme each year (184 in the last 18 months), in about ten groups. Detecting a rise in completion from 41 to 55 percent with 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 would need about 200 starters per period before allowing for clustering by group; with an intraclass correlation of about 0.05 and groups of eleven, about 300 per period would be needed, which the clinic will not reach in 2027. The study is therefore not powered for a confirmatory comparison. Completion is tracked group by group on a run chart against the baseline median, and reach and outcomes are reported descriptively with confidence intervals.
primaryAnalysis: Run chart of completion by group against the baseline median, with pre-specified rules for a shift and adaptation start dates marked; completion by employment, travel mode and language reported with 95 percent confidence intervals.
secondaryAnalysis: Reach by quarter; pain interference change for completers and leavers; group connection and fidelity by adaptation; framework analysis of conversations with leavers mapped to CFIR constructs.
missingData: Missing follow-up is reported by group and by whether the person completed; no imputation for the implementation outcomes, which are recorded for everyone.
multiplicity: One primary implementation outcome; all other measures are descriptive.
software: Spreadsheet run chart and R for confidence intervals.
overfittingGuards: Run chart rules fixed before the first 2027 group
No subgroup testing beyond the three recorded barriers
summary: Not powered for a confirmatory comparison; completion tracked on a run chart with descriptive reach and outcomes.
